title: Objective synthesis handoff and cross-team commitment register
creator: Avery Chen
description: Goal: Create a repeatable, auditable handoff process that converts company-level OKR statements into explicit initiative commitments with named owners, success criteria, and cross-team dependency registers. This ticket scopes the definition of the handoff template, the lightweight governance process (who reviews and signs off), and the register mechanism that will live alongside Linear issues and the company roadmap dashboard. Outcomes: 1) a one-page handoff template that PMs use to convert objectives into initiatives; 2) a cross-team commitments register (searchable, exportable CSV + Linear tags) capturing owner, dependency type, risk level, and sign-off; 3) a lightweight cadence (triage and sign-off meetings) and escalation path for blocked commitments.
acceptance_criteria: Handoff template in Confluence and Drive with fields: objective mapping, hypothesis, measurable success metrics, rollout gates, primary owner, dependent teams, risks & mitigations, expected launch window
Commitments register prototype implemented as a Google Sheet + CSV export and a Linear saved view that lists commitment-tagged issues
Pilot run completed with 3 cross-functional initiatives from Q2 roadmap and documented outcomes
Stakeholders (Eng, Design, Security, GTM) have signed the governance doc and cadence schedule
Guidance doc for PMs on how to break an objective into initiatives and estimate capacity is reviewed and published
notes: Principle: keep the handoff light-weight to avoid introducing waterfall overhead — focus on clarity and traceability.
We will use existing Linear fields where possible (project, labels, parent_issue) and add a new label 'commitment:yes' to mark tickets that are signed commitments against company objectives.
Consider adding a 'commitment owner' custom field in Linear if stakeholders find label-based tracking insufficient — escalate after pilot.
Design has suggested a matrix view (owner vs dependent teams) that can be exported as SVG for leadership decks. Low effort MVP: table export from Google Sheet.

risks: Risk: Overhead — too much structure will slow PM velocity and lead teams to avoid tagging commitments. Mitigation: keep fields minimal for pilot.
Risk: Ownership ambiguity — if owners are not explicitly named and have no time allocation, commitments become soft. Mitigation: require primary and secondary owners and an estimated capacity delta.

Risk: Tooling mismatch — Linear labels may not capture multi-dimensional dependency attributes. Mitigation: prototype with Google Sheet and validate; evaluate adding a Linear custom field after pilot.
